recipes.name: Spinach Stuffed Mushrooms
ingredients_raw: 30 large whole fresh mushrooms, stems removed
salt and ground black pepper to taste
1 (10 ounce) package frozen chopped spinach, thawed and drained

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Lightly grease 30 muffin cups with olive oil. Brush all sides mushrooms with remaining olive oil; place gill-sides-up into the prepared muffin cups.
Bake in the preheated oven until mushrooms just tender, about 12 minutes.
Meanwhile, beat egg, garlic, salt, and black pepper together in a bowl; stir in spinach, 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese, Gouda cheese, mozzarella cheese, and bread crumbs until evenly combined.
Remove mushrooms from oven; drain and discard any accumulated juice. Fill mushroom caps with spinach mixture; return to the muffin cups. Sprinkle mushrooms with remaining 1/4 cup Parmesan cheese.
Bake until stuffing is hot and golden brown, about 10 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach Stuffed Mushrooms
raw_recipe.description: This recipe for savory spinach-stuffed mushrooms includes a cheesy bread crumb filling made with three types of cheese: Gouda, mozzarella, and Parmesan.

review.reviewBody: I made a little change and used smoked gouda to give it a little change in the taste. Got rave reviews. Thanks for the recipe!!!

This is a very basic recipe that with a little tweaking can be an awesome recipe. I halved the recipe because I only had 20 mushrooms of various sizes. The filling as written was dry and tasteless. I added 4 oz of cream cheese, Mrs Dash herb & garlic and shallots that I sauteed, I also omitted the salt. I laid the mushrooms on a parchment paper lined cookie sheet, sprayed lightly with baking spray and baked for 10 minutes, flipped them over, filled and baked for 20 minutes, they were the first to go at our neighbourhood open house.
#AllrecipesAllstarsCanada
#ChristmasHosting

I tweaked this a little based on what I had available and personal taste, but it turned out fantastic. I didn't have Gouda, so I substituted Asiago. I doubled the garlic and added 2 oz cream cheese because I knew I wanted mine to be very cheesy and one review mentioned they were dry. When I filled the mushrooms, I brushed a bit of melted butter over the mix before I sprinkled on the final Parmesan. I actually had a little filling leftover, so I'm stuffing a couple portobellas for dinner tonight that I will serve with pasta and red sauce like a "stuffed portobello parmesan" The whole tray of these mushrooms disappeared in no time at the potluck. You'll be so glad you made these.

The wife and I both loved this recipe/base. My variations were using Costco fresh mushrooms (some of which were 4-inches in diameter), fresh Kroger bagged spinach (boiled a minute or so until tender), shredded mozzarella and grated parmesian cheese and for the final baking, I covered the stuffed mushrooms with Sargento Light Swiss cheese.
Good, but the mix is a little dry. I added 1/2 cup of Hellman's mayo to the mix. It moistened it, and improved the taste a lot.

I used the basic recipe as an inspiration. I think you can start with the spinach and some kind of cheese - if using a hard cheese I would add in something to make it creamy (I used cottage cheese to keep the calorie count down). Saute everything before filling.

Absolutely wonderful! I didn't have gouda cheese, so i used some extra italian blend cheeses and fresh chopped spinach (no need to saute). I used 12 extra large mushrooms with the full recipe, can't wait to make them again!

I had part of a package of mushrooms to use up (8 mushrooms) and a couple handfuls of fresh spinach so I halved the recipe. I quickly sauteed the spinach and then mixed in the remaining ingredients. I used mozzarella, parmesan and rosemary asiago cheese (didn't have gouda). I've never mixed an egg in mushroom stuffing before and I was skeptical but they are good! I didn't sprinkle the additional cheese over the top - seemed like overkill to me. I also used seasoned Panko bread crumbs instead of regular. I will make these again!

I made it and added a 1/2 cup of vegetarian meatless meat -TVP and the Gouda cheese had jalapeño bits and it was amazing. Also diced the mushroom stems after cutting off hard stem ends. I got both tips from others plus a similar recipe! My wife loved them so much she went out two days later, bought the ingredients and tried to repeat...LOL.
This was a very simple recipe. I didn't add the breadcrumbs and cooked sliced mushrooms in the recipe and put it on fish. My family loved it!

I am so glad that hese were so simple to put together because they were gobbled up very quickly! I followed the recipe with only one change, I added some finely diced red bell pepper for color. I will definitely be making more of these!
Very easy, tasty, and we put this on our favorite list ! We used fresh spinach & chopped by hand ; may pulse spinach in a blender next time so that the mixture is more compact but not necessary.

I liked it, especially the low calorie count. I would probably use more cheese next time.
Thanks!

great when you on a diet.
This was just what I was looking for. I used a 3 cheese blend of Asiago, Romano, and Parmesan . Otherwise , I followed the recipe. very good.

I followed the directions pretty closely, except I used fresh garlic instead of from a jar. The flavor was very nice, but they were a ittle dry. I will make these again, but I will add a bit of cream cheese to moisten them up a bit.
I made these and they were amazing! We make these all the time for our bbq's in the summer time along with Jalapeno poppers and they just turn out fabulous !

This is the best mushroom appetizer ! I have taken this to several covered dish parties and everyone keeps asking me for the recipe. My family also loves this and keeps asking me to make it as side dish with steaks and chops. I sometimes substitute Asiago cheese just for a change. Thanks for the great recipe.
